table_i_l1_cache_get.description: 10,000 sequential cache.get() calls on the L1 memory tier. No routing, no auth, no serialization, no network.
table_i_l1_cache_get.caveat: The harness measures with a 1 µs timer, so a reported P50 of 0 means 'below one microsecond', not zero cost.

table_ii_gateway_stack.description: 5,000 sequential requests through the full Axum stack: API-key auth, routing, JCS canonicalization, exact-cache admission. In-process via tower::ServiceExt::oneshot, so no TCP or TLS.

notes: This is the source of the 14,202.9 req/s / P50 0.068 ms / P99 0.144 ms figures previously attributed in the docs to the multi-worker soak test. Those figures were produced here, by this test, on a slightly different run (this run measures 13,241.1 req/s at the same P50, about 7% lower). The soak test produces different, higher-latency numbers because it drives 16 concurrent workers instead of a sequential loop.
Both tables are single-machine, in-process measurements. A real deployment adds a network hop, TLS termination, and often a proxy, all of which raise latency.
Re-run the command above; absolute values depend on the machine. The ratio between the L1 tier and the full stack is the useful quantity.
